received_feedback: More breathing room; explain broader vision rather than narrow supply-risk example
prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual / precise reference-led redesign.
Rework the supplied two reference layouts into ONE SINGLE 16:9 English pitch slide for the operational-intelligence product described below.
Input image 1 is a COMPOSITION AND SPACING REFERENCE ONLY: an airy white page, a measured refined headline, three feature areas with product UI fragments, generous gaps and a restrained footer. Input image 2 is a TYPE HIERARCHY AND PRODUCT-CARD STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: light background, elegant medium-weight headline, very restrained mint accent, clear short text and carefully cropped miniature product views.
Replace ALL source wording, source logos, brands, claims and UI subject matter. This is an adaptation of the reference layout to our own product, not a slide about MCP, profiling, calls, Claude, Cursor or Calldesk.
Output only the full-bleed slide, no blue external surround, no webpage browser, no perspective, no laptop, no framing canvas. Landscape 16:9. Make it feel authored by a good SaaS product designer, relaxed and explanatory, never a consulting report.

PRODUCT VISION:
Help companies dependent on inventory and supply ecosystems adapt to external change. An agent monitors industry/public/regional signals, relates evidence to the company's sites, stock, suppliers and customers, identifies risks AND opportunities, investigates missing information, calculates options and prepares a revisable human decision. New facts lead to reassessment. Timber/materials is the first market, not the whole vision. No ERP/CRM connector, commercial opportunity calculation or scaled deployment is claimed as delivered.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
Lots of real whitespace. White or very pale neutral background, near-black/charcoal typography, deep petrol teal and restrained soft mint accents. One refined sans serif, normal/medium weights as in references, never huge extra-bold block text. Main headline comfortable two lines, about 58-68 px at 1920-wide, not consuming the canvas. The three product columns should be well-spaced, each with one short title, one short sentence, and one small purpose-built UI fragment that explains the step. Very pale grey feature surfaces with thin borders or no borders, quiet micro-shadows allowed on the UI fragments. No robots, network spaghetti, clipart icons, factory illustrations, 3D scenes, heavy tables, dark full-width color fields, loud gradients or random decoration. If adding soft mint tint, confine it to a small part of a product fragment. The UI fragments have only a few legible lines; they are proposed product visuals, not screenshots proving the current app.
Leave a generous margin of around 96px; keep clear vertical breathing space between headline, three-feature area and footer. The slide should be absorbable in a few seconds.

EXACT ENGLISH COPY, NO EXTRA PARAGRAPHS:
Small descriptor above main headline:
"OPERATIONAL INTELLIGENCE"
Main headline in two balanced lines:
"Help businesses adapt"
"to market changes."
Subtitle, no longer than two lines:
"Connect industry signals with company data to reveal risks, opportunities and workable next steps."

Three feature columns:
Column 1 title: "Watch the market"
Body: "News, public data and changes across your industry."
Its UI fragment: a beautifully typeset little source feed, with just the labels
"Sector update"
"Regional project"
"Supplier announcement"
Small neutral status "Source received"

Column 2 title: "Know what matters"
Body: "Find the links to your operations, commitments and customers."
Its UI fragment: concise company-context header "Company context", a tiny text row "Sites   Stock   Suppliers   Customers", then two clear restrained rows:
"Risk to assess"
"Opportunity to qualify"
These are investigation targets, not established commercial impacts. Use a soft amber accent on risk and a soft green accent on opportunity. Do not fabricate counts or numerical impact.

Column 3 title: "Prepare the response"
Body: "Calculate options, review a proposal and revisit it when facts change."
Its UI fragment: a sober proposed decision view titled "Options to review" with only:
"Request confirmation"
"Compare alternatives"
and one quiet petrol action labelled "Review proposal"
No approved or executed status.

Under a very light horizontal rule, keep three compact open footer columns:
"WHO"
"Operations teams with stock and supply-chain dependencies."
"WHY NOW"
"Agents combine investigation with checked business calculations."
"FIRST USERS"
"Plan: 3 design partners in French timber and materials."

One final small readable line, visually quiet but not microscopic:
"Product concept. Prototype: real tools and Aiven PostgreSQL on synthetic data. Benchmark pending."

Text accuracy is essential. All text in English. No em dash. Do not add a working brand name, invented URL, QR code, integration logos, market numbers, savings, customer logos or evidence graphs. No brand has been selected. The first-user line is a proposed plan, not acquired customers.
The three product blocks should carry the explanation visually and be genuinely useful, not be empty decorative cards. Give risk and opportunity equal visible status. Preserve the broad company-adaptation promise, not an emergency procurement-only pitch.
